title: ～がち — tends to ～ (usually undesirable)
summary: A suffix meaning something tends to happen or is often the case, mostly used for undesirable things. It attaches to the stem of a verb (ます-form without ます) or to a noun.

body.p: With verbs, drop ます from the polite form (休み, 忘れ, なり). Nouns are state words such as 病気 or 留守. Typical forms: ～がちだ, ～がちの＋noun, ～がちな＋noun.
It points out a regrettable tendency: 'it easily turns out that way.' It is normally not used for good things (勉強がち is wrong). The key idea is repetition or tendency, not a one-time event.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）は最近（さいきん）学校（がっこう）を休（やす）みがちだ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa saikin gakkō o yasumigachi da.
examples.tr: He tends to be absent from school lately.

examples.ja: 冬（ふゆ）は運動（うんどう）が不足（ふそく）しがちだ。
examples.romaji: Fuyu wa undō ga fusoku shigachi da.
examples.tr: In winter we tend to lack exercise.

examples.ja: 忙（いそが）しいと、食事（しょくじ）がいい加減（かげん）になりがちだ。
examples.romaji: Isogashii to, shokuji ga iikagen ni narigachi da.
examples.tr: When you're busy, meals tend to become careless.

pitfalls: Do not keep ます: 休みがち, not 休みますがち.
It is for undesirable tendencies. Saying 'tends to study hard' with がち sounds odd.
